summary: Michael W. Charney works in history and archaeology. He earned his PhD from the University of Michigan in 1999 and became Professor of Asian and Military History at SOAS University of London in 2001.

Michael W. Meister is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Harvard University (BA 1964, MA 1971, PhD 1974) and the University of Pennsylvania, where he became a professor around 1976, succeeding Stella Kramrisch.

Michael Weiers was a linguist and Central Asian studies scholar. He completed his dissertation at the University of Bonn around 1965, later serving there as professor from 1972 to 2003 and as an honorary professor at Inner Mongolia University around 1993.

Michael Wenger is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at The New School (MA) and under Mel Weitsman. He served as Dean of Buddhist Studies at San Francisco Zen Center and founded Dragons Leap Meditation Center, serving as guiding teacher.

Michael Willis works in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied under Siri Gunasinghe and Alan Gowans at the University of Victoria (BA) and under J. A. B. van Buitenen and Pramod Chandra at the University of Chicago (doctoral degree, 1988). He was Curator at the British Museum (1994–2014).

Michael Witzel is an Indologist and linguist. He studied under Karl Hoffmann, Paul Thieme, Hanns-Peter Schmidt, Johanna Narten, Jununath Pandit, and F. B. J. Kuiper. He held the Sanskrit Chair at Leiden University (1978–1986) before moving to Harvard in 1986.
Michael Yorke studied at Yale University as a graduate student (attested 2026) and held a post there in Religious Studies.

Michael Zimmermann works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and others, also studying at Soka University. He held posts at Stanford (2003) and Hamburg (professor from ~2007).

Michael von Brück is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Rostock and the University of Madras. He held professorships at the University of Regensburg (1988–1991) and the University of Munich (~1991–2014).

Michaela Haas is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Bonn under Peter Schwieger (attested 2008) and also studied under Rechungpa and Jigme Namgyal Dzigar Kongtrul.

Michaela Mross specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. She studied at Komazawa University and the University of Munich (PhD, 2014). She held posts at UC Berkeley and the University of Göttingen before becoming Assistant Professor at Stanford University in 2016.

Michaël Peyrot is a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at Leiden University (1999–2010) and held posts at Leiden University (~2012, 2016) and the Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (2014–2016).

Michel Bitbol specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under Pierre Mills and at Paris Diderot University (-1985). He has held positions at CNRS (~1997, 2020), the University of Paris, Linacre College, Oxford, and Paris 1 Pantheon-Sorbonne.

Michel Bréal was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at École Normale Supérieure and Humboldt University under Albrecht Weber and Franz Bopp. He held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, Collège de France (1864–1905), and École Pratique des Hautes Études (1868–1882).

Michel Clasquin-Johnson is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He completed his studies, including his doctoral thesis, at the University of South Africa (-1999), where he also held a post beginning in 1990.

Michel Hulin is a philosopher and Indologist. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure (1956) and Paris-Sorbonne University under Olivier Lacombe, later holding a post at Paris-Sorbonne University from 1981 to 1998.

Michel Jacq-Hergoualc'h was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Jean Boisselier in 1988 and served as a professor at Sorbonne Nouvelle University from around 1990 to 2008.
Michel Ledrus was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He held posts at KU Leuven (1931), the Pontifical Gregorian University (1932–1933), and Collegio Bellarmino (1949).

Michel Lejeune was a linguist. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure (~1926–1929) and under Antoine Meillet. His career included posts at the University of Poitiers (~1933–1937), University of Paris (~1947–1955), and École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1951–1975).

Michel Mohr specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He earned his PhD at the University of Geneva and studied under Seizan Yanagida. He held posts at Geneva, Hanazono University (attested 2000–2006), and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (2007).
